questions.scenario: A coastal rescue center wants to estimate the average time that its trained volunteer crews spend at sea each week. It records times for 45 of its crews.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the population of interest?
choices: All trained volunteer crews at the rescue center
All coastal residents
All employees of the rescue center
All trained volunteer crews in the country

steps: The goal concerns trained volunteer crews belonging to this rescue center.
The 45 observed crews form a sample. The population includes all crews meeting the goal's definition.
solution.warning: Keep both restrictions: trained volunteer crews and membership in this center.

questions.scenario: A regional ferry operator wants to study passengers who buy monthly passes. It can contact monthly-pass holders, single-ticket buyers, terminal employees, and nearby residents.
questions.prompt: Which group consists entirely of members of the target population?
choices: 80 monthly-pass holders selected from the operator's records
80 nearby residents selected from an address list
80 passengers selected from all ticket buyers
80 terminal employees selected from a staff list

steps: Every member of the sample must belong to the defined population of monthly-pass holders.
Only the sample drawn from monthly-pass records guarantees that membership.
solution.warning: A group that might include pass holders is not guaranteed to be a subset of them.

questions.scenario: A repair service records the model, repair time, and replacement cost for each of 120 electric scooters.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is an observational unit?
choices: One electric scooter
The repair service's spreadsheet
The average replacement cost
The repair time

steps: An observational unit is the object on which measurements are taken.
Each scooter has a model, repair time, and replacement cost recorded.
solution.warning: A variable is a characteristic measured on a unit; a summary combines measurements.

questions.scenario: A maintenance team records measurements and counts for each park fountain.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a continuous quantitative variable?

The number of lamps around the fountain
The number of pumps installed

questions.scenario: A random sample of 160 parcels from a warehouse has a mean mass of 2.8 kilograms. The mean mass of all parcels shipped from the warehouse that day is unknown.
questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the value 2.8?
choices: A parameter, because it describes every parcel shipped that day.
An individual measurement, because each parcel has a mass.
A parameter, because it summarizes the sampled parcels.
A statistic, because it summarizes the sampled parcels.

steps: A statistic summarizes a sample; a parameter summarizes the entire population.
The value 2.8 kilograms was calculated from the 160 sampled parcels.
solution.warning: The type of summary depends on which units were measured, not on whether the value is known.

questions.scenario: A theater checks every one of its 850 seats and finds that 4% need repair.
questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the 4%?
choices: A parameter, because all seats in this theater were checked.
A statistic, because percentages are always sample summaries.
An observational unit, because it describes a seat.
A statistic, because fewer than all theaters were checked.

steps: The population for this investigation is all 850 seats in this theater.
Checking every seat gives a population proportion, which is a parameter.
solution.warning: Define the population from the study's goal. It does not automatically include other theaters.

questions.scenario: A transit agency will survey a random sample of registered bicycle-parking users to determine whether a majority want covered parking.
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the appropriate investigative question?
choices: How many bicycles does a typical registered user own?
Do more than half of the surveyed users want covered parking?
Does one randomly selected user want covered parking?
Do more than half of all registered bicycle-parking users want covered parking?

steps: The goal concerns the population proportion of registered users who want covered parking.
A majority means more than half, and the conclusion concerns all registered users rather than only the sample.
solution.warning: An investigative question must preserve the population, variable, and direction of the study.

questions.scenario: A community garden recorded one preferred volunteer task for each participant. The counts are shown in the table.
questions.prompt: What proportion of participants preferred planting?

steps: The four counts total 80 participants.

questions.scenario: A craft fair recorded the main material used by each of its 100 stalls. The counts are shown in the table.
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is supported by the table?
choices: Wood was the most common main material.
Exactly 25% of the stalls primarily used metal.
Exactly 40% of the stalls primarily used fabric.
There were 120 stalls in total.

steps: Add the counts: 25 + 40 + 15 + 20 = 100.
Fabric accounts for 40 of 100 stalls. Wood is not the largest category, and metal accounts for 15%.
solution.warning: A count becomes a percentage only after dividing by the total.

questions.scenario: A marine center recorded the preferred tour of each of 120 visitors. The results are shown in the table.
questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is <u>not</u> supported by the table?
choices: One-sixth preferred a harbor tour.
One-fourth preferred a kayak tour.
One-third preferred a reef tour.
Kayak and reef tours together account for half the visitors.

steps: Kayak and reef tours together account for 30 + 40 = 70 visitors.
Half of 120 is 60, so the combined share is greater than half. The other three fractions match their counts.
solution.warning: For a not-supported question, reject the one claim contradicted by the counts.

questions.scenario: At two festivals, visitors each chose one favorite activity. The results are shown in the table.
questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly compares the proportion choosing the climbing wall?
choices: It was higher at Hill: 45/150 exceeds 60/240.
It was higher at Hill because 150 is smaller than 240.
It was equal because both festivals offered the same activity.
It was higher at Lake because 60 exceeds 45.

steps: Hill's climbing-wall share is 45/150 = 0.30; Lake's is 60/240 = 0.25.
Hill has the larger proportion, although Lake has the larger count.
solution.warning: Different group sizes require each count to be divided by its own total.

questions.scenario: A dispatch office recorded the distance in kilometers for each delivery. The histogram shows the distances.
questions.prompt: Which of the following descriptions is supported by the histogram?
choices: The distribution is approximately normal with no isolated values.
The isolated delivery was from 20 to under 25 kilometers.
The distribution has no gaps between its occupied intervals.
Most deliveries were under 20 kilometers, with an isolated delivery from 35 to under 40 kilometers.

steps: All but one delivery lie below 20 kilometers.
The intervals from 20 to under 35 are empty, separating the delivery in the last bin from the main group.
solution.warning: An empty interval is a gap; a distant occupied interval can indicate a potential outlier.
